articles.title: APPLE EXPLORES SHAKING UP ITS SMARTWATCH FOR A NEW ERA
articles.summary: The Apple Watch continues to attract new buyers and remains the top-selling smartwatch. However, the company's industrial design team has been exploring a broad rethink of Apple's smartwatches and is evaluating several different directions. Apple needs to adapt to the rise of screenless fitness bands and smart rings, which are cheaper, lighter, and more fun and convenient to use for many people. The company aims to inject new life into its Wearables, Home, and Accessories segment, which has struggled to generate meaningful growth in recent years.

articles.title: NOW WE HAVE A TIMELINE OF THE OPENAI ACCIDENTAL ATTACK AGAINST HUGGING FACE
articles.summary: OpenAI recently gave a presentation about the Hugging Face incident. The talk is short and information dense and provides full details of what happened and how things played out inside OpenAI. This post presents the timeline of events and details how the hack occurred. A video of the presentation is available in the post.

articles.title: THE FIRST SELF-DRIVING VEHICLE ON MARS HAS PROVEN TO BE A SMASHING SUCCESS
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance Mars rover will set a record for the most distance driven by any vehicle on another world sometime next week. The rover's auto navigation system has enabled about 90% of the distance driven by the vehicle to be autonomous. Not having to wait for navigation commands from drivers on Earth has allowed the rover to maximize the amount of scientific return. The vehicle will likely be able to keep driving itself across Mars for many years to come.

articles.title: CHINA-FREE BATTERIES MADE FROM SALT ARE FINALLY HERE
articles.summary: Peak Energy, a US-based startup, has raised tens of millions of dollars to build a factory for its sodium-ion battery packs. It already has more than $1.1 billion in announced deals with customers. Sodium batteries have less-intensive cooling needs than lithium-ion packs, and they are less likely to catch fire. Another US-based startup, Inlyte Energy, is working on another type of sodium-based battery that can't catch fire at all.

articles.title: AGENTIC CODE QUALITY
articles.summary: Software quality now depends on the constraints set around the agents that wrote it. Constraints define what a system is allowed to do. Setting and maintaining these constraints allows developers to build loops that reliably deliver high-quality production software. Agents can propose anything - constraints decide whether a proposal is safe enough, correct, scoped, and useful.

articles.title: GOOGLE'S WESTINGHOUSE BET
articles.summary: Google's recent reshuffling of its AI operations has many thinking that the company has failed in the AI race. However, the company may just be refocusing its resources on its strengths. Google Cloud may be a much larger economic opportunity than pursuing its rivals in the frontier AI race. The company's enormous distribution advantage means it doesn't have to compete in the expensive and unprofitable frontier race.

articles.title: AMAZON CRACKS DOWN ON 'CPU WASTE' AMONG ENGINEERS AS AGENTIC AI CRUNCH INTENSIFIES
articles.summary: AWS is cracking down on internal use of EC2 instances among its engineers. Engineers have been told to reduce CPU waste to ensure the company has enough CPU capacity to meet customer demand. The increased demand for CPU is due to the rise of AI agentic workloads. Other cloud companies are also seeing high demand for CPUs.

articles.title: CHANGING DEVTOOLS IS CHEAP. OWNING THEM ISN'T
articles.summary: The future of software will be powered by high-quality, well-documented building blocks that users can build specialized artifacts on top of. Agents are good at composing high-quality components. Maintainers can provide these components alongside a focus application, and users can choose how to modify their experiences themselves. This allows software to be personalized while still being developed by maintainers that care.

articles.summary: Revision Prompting supplies LLMs with the original input, the original output, and the changes to the input, and instructs it to produce a patch that updates the original output accordingly.
